_meta.purpose: Ground truth for the FindCNG 'Ask about CNG' chat. Every fact below comes from the project's public sentiment evidence base (CNG-PUBLIC-SENTIMENT.md, 17 Nov 2026) or the app's own dataset (data/stats.json, 18 Nov 2026). Nothing here is invented. Each fact group carries its source and date; the chat must date prices and never present a fact without its source.

facts.source: NADDC / SON / Pi-CNG findings and Punch, BusinessDay, Nairametrics reporting, Oct 2024 – Nov 2026
facts.text: A certified CNG system, professionally installed by an accredited centre, is safe. Every investigated incident traces to uncertified equipment or unqualified installation — fake or welded cylinders, LPG cooking-gas cylinders, air-conditioner cylinders, or overfilling — never to a certified automotive CNG system. CNG ignites at about 700°C vs petrol at about 455°C, so it needs much more heat to catch fire. CNG is lighter than air: if it leaks, it rises and disperses instead of pooling on the ground like petrol. Certified cylinders are multi-layer steel or composite and pressure-tested. Cylinders must be tested every 3 years.

facts.source: SON; NADDC; Kaduna police; Pi-CNG; Punch / BusinessDay / New Daily Prime / LASTMA
facts.text: Benin City, 16-17 Oct 2024: cylinder fabricated by a local welder from scrap metal — welded, modified, not approved for CNG. 3 people severely injured (one leg amputated); the welder was arrested. Abuja Airport Road, 13 Sep 2026: unapproved, unsuitable auxiliary cylinder fitted to a Toyota Camry, which exploded while refuelling (NADDC preliminary finding); no deaths. Kaduna, Apr 2026: Kaduna police preliminary findings linked a bus explosion to overfilling; the operator disputes this, a multi-agency probe was ordered, and no final finding has been published as of 18 Nov 2026 — the cause is NOT settled. Sep 2026, undisclosed location: owner fitted an air-conditioner cylinder as a CNG cylinder, using AC pipe; car destroyed, no lives lost. Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, 11 Nov 2026: gas explosion in a bus (18 occupants); exact technical cause under investigation at the time of reporting; 17 rescued unhurt, 1 severe burns. Banex, Abuja, 3 Oct 2025: CNG car caught fire; cause disputed — some eyewitnesses said electrical fault, not CNG; no casualties.
facts.topic: safety: incident causes in plain words

facts.source: Pi-CNG / NADDC guidance; Minister Ekperikpe Ekpo; safety expert Toheeb Adisa (Independent, 14 Nov 2026); LASTMA GM Olalekan Bakare-Oki (11 Nov 2026)
facts.text: Convert only at an accredited centre and ask to see its NADDC/Pi-CNG accreditation certificate and the cylinder's certification markings. Never accept a welded, second-hand or cooking-gas cylinder. Make sure the engine is in good condition before converting — CNG reveals existing engine problems. Get the cylinder tested every 3 years and prioritise regular professional inspections. If you smell gas or hear hissing: switch off, get out of the vehicle, move away, and go to an accredited centre. Never try to fix a gas system yourself.
facts.topic: safety: what to do and what never to do

facts.source: Punch, 3 Sep 2025; Pulse; Nairametrics / Punch, Sep-Nov 2026
facts.text: CNG: ₦380 per SCM for cars and buses, ₦450 per SCM for trucks — the price since September 2025, when the Federal Government withdrew subsidy support (it was ₦230 per SCM before that). Petrol: ₦1,330-₦1,405 per litre as reported November 2026. At ₦380, CNG is roughly 70-75% cheaper than petrol per unit of energy. Drivers consistently report 50-75% fuel-cost savings. Prices move — always give the date with any price.

facts.source: Pi-CNG / State House videos; NURTW; Nairametrics; ThinkBusiness Africa
facts.text: Abuja taxi driver (160 km/day): about ₦22,000/day on petrol to about ₦6,000/day on CNG, about ₦412,000/month saved. Keke operator: ₦15,000-17,000/day to ₦3,500-4,000/day. Lagos Bolt driver: ₦10,000-15,000 by midday on petrol to ₦30,000-40,000 by midday on CNG. Note: several testimonials come from Pi-CNG/State House promotional videos, which select their best cases — but independent forum and news-interview figures point in the same direction.

facts.source: Pi-CNG FAQ (pci.gov.ng); BusinessDay, Oct 2026; Leadership, 6 Nov 2026
facts.text: Official Pi-CNG ranges: cars ₦350,000-₦600,000; buses/vans ₦450,000-₦800,000; keke ₦180,000-₦280,000. Market prices run higher: ₦650,000-₦2,500,000 depending on vehicle, kit and centre. Financing: CALM Fund financing at 9% exists but is poorly known; a 50% government subsidy on kits was offered in June 2024; free conversions for commercial vehicles began in Abuja/Lagos in July 2024. Pi-CNG's FAQ says conversion is typically recovered in 6-12 months of regular use — but drivers who queue 3-4 hours daily say the payback maths breaks.

facts.source: Pi-CNG / Federal Ministry of Finance briefing, 8 Oct 2026; Pi-CNG registers; Punch, 16 Nov 2026
facts.text: Pi-CNG & EV (Presidential CNG Initiative, expanded to include EVs in March 2026) runs the federal CNG programme; NADDC accredits conversion centres and runs the 300-corps-member CNG retrofitting training programme. About 120,000-140,000 vehicles converted; about 105 operational refuelling stations on the Pi-CNG register (updated 15 Oct 2026, 24 states + FCT) — roughly 1,300 vehicles per station. 300+ accredited conversion centres (mid-2026). 127 more refuelling stations reported in development (Nov 2026). President Tinubu ordered 500 additional stations and set a target of 1 million CNG vehicles by 2027. Pi-CNG & EV Executive Chairman Ismaeel Ahmed admitted on 16 Nov 2026 that high conversion costs and inadequate stations are slowing adoption.

facts.source: Saturday PUNCH, 31 Oct 2026; Nairametrics, 20 Sep 2026; The Sun, Sep 2026; BusinessDay, Oct 2026
facts.text: Queues of 3-6 hours are common; some drivers sleep at stations. Only 10 stations serve Abuja. Low pressure often means a half-fill even after hours of queuing, and broken compressors stop supply entirely (one Abuja NIPCO outlet reportedly did not sell CNG for about 3 months because of a faulty compressor). In Minna, Niger State, converted motorists protested after more than three months without CNG at the NNPC Mega Station. Officials have promised queues will 'disappear by December' — a promise met with open scepticism.

facts.source: Pi-CNG FAQ; Nairametrics; Nairaland; Kfat33 Autos, Jul 2026
facts.text: Pi-CNG's official position: slight power reduction of typically 3-8%; most drivers find acceleration smooth. In practice, some converted cars jerk or lose power, need plugs and coils changed more often, and are hard to start in the morning — usually from poor installation, poor calibration, or an engine that was already weak. Proper calibration and good iridium plugs fix many cases. CNG does not manage a bad engine: it reveals even small existing issues. Some owners have removed their kits ('dekitting') and switched back to petrol.

facts.source: NSChE magazine; TechCabal, Aug 2026; Carlots.ng; Legit.ng, 26 Oct 2026
facts.text: The cylinder occupies most of the boot; a steel Type-1 cylinder weighs 60-80 kg when full. Range is about 80 km per fill in one cited case, and low-pressure half-fills make it worse. Unlike petrol, you cannot buy CNG in a jerrycan or borrow some on the highway — refuelling must be planned around stations, which makes inter-state trips harder. Conversion can affect resale value: some buyers like the fuel savings, others prefer an unmodified vehicle — keep installation records and maintenance documents.

facts.source: Punch state-by-state check, Oct 2026; OpenLife/Punch, 31 Oct 2026
facts.text: President Tinubu directed on 19 Sep 2026 that CNG savings should reach passengers as lower fares by 1 Oct 2026; Punch found it was not implemented in 14 states, including Edo. Drivers say they keep fares high to recover conversion costs and lost queue hours. Counter-example: Kaduna CNG buses saved commuters ₦3.5bn in a year, and Lagos-Ibadan fares dropped from ₦8,000 to ₦3,200 on CNG buses.

facts.source: FindCNG dataset (data/stats.json, generated 18 Nov 2026) and app documentation
facts.text: FindCNG Nigeria is a free, no-account web app built by ED/26B/2316, a serving NYSC corps member in the NADDC-NYSC CNG Retrofitting Training Programme (Edo State, 1 of 300), as his Community Development Service (CDS) project. It lists 663 records: 129 refuelling locations and 564 conversion centres across 29 states + FCT (8 states have no data yet). 525 centres are matched on the Pi-CNG accredited centres register (checked 18 Nov 2026); 105 refuelling locations match the Pi-CNG refuelling register (updated 15 Oct 2026). Drivers report live gas availability — reports expire after 2 hours so old information never misleads. The Centres tab checks any installer against the Pi-CNG accredited list. The Safety hub explains certified-vs-fake in English and Pidgin. The calculator compares CNG vs petrol with the user's own numbers. The route planner plans refuelling stops along a drive.

facts.source: NIPOST postcode system; FindCNG app documentation
facts.text: Nigeria's postcode system has two formats: the old 6-digit area codes (for example 300001 for Benin City GPO) and the new 11-character digital postcodes launched 1 October 2026 (for example FC 02 A09 DB 09), which identify one building. A 6-digit code covers a whole district, so it only centres the map approximately. NIPOST does not give out building coordinates through its API, so an 11-character code alone never produces a map point — the app asks for GPS or a map tap for the exact spot. Anyone can find their building's code free at postcode.gov.ng/find.

Benin City is where Nigeria's CNG story started (NIPCO since 2009) and has the highest concentration of conversion workshops of any Nigerian city. But Benin is also where the most traumatic CNG incident happened: the October 2024 Aduwawa explosion (fake welded cylinder, 3 severely injured, one leg amputated). The Diverse Autocare CNG hub on Sapele Road was commissioned in May 2026 by the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas). Fonnd Motor on Airport Road is the project builder's current attachment.
